objective: Build a text adventure game in Python that is genuinely fun to play. The engine loads world data from YAML files defining rooms, items, NPCs, monsters, and connections. Implement a command parser handling movement (go north/south/east/west), inventory management (take, drop, use, examine), NPC interaction (talk to), combat commands (attack, flee), and look/status/help/quit. Add a turn-based combat system: the player has health and attack power, weapons and armor found in the world change combat stats when equipped, healing items can be used mid-fight, and monsters guard specific rooms and fight back with simple distinct behaviors. Include a final boss with two phases and a weakness to a special item hidden in the world — beating the boss wins the game, and dying ends the run with an honest defeat screen and the option to restart. Manage game state including player location, stats, equipment, inventory, room state changes, NPC dialogue progression, and defeated monsters. Support save and load of full game state to JSON. Create a playable demo world with at least 8 rooms, 5 items (including at least one weapon, one armor piece, one healing item, and the boss-weakness item), 2 NPCs with branching dialogue that hints at the boss weakness, 3 regular monsters, and the final boss. The game must be runnable from the command line, produce engaging descriptive text with clear combat narration, and be winnable in a reasonable playthrough by following the NPC hints.

notes.content:
Use `yaml.safe_load()` exclusively to avoid arbitrary code execution vulnerabilities when loading world data. Structure YAML files with clear hierarchies: rooms as top-level keys containing connections, items, NPCs, and monsters as nested dictionaries—this maps naturally to Python objects via `dataclasses` or `NamedTuple` for type safety and clean serialization. For save/load, use JSON with atomic writes (`os.replace()`) and include a version field to handle future schema changes; store saves in platform-appropriate directories (use `platformdirs`).

For the command parser, adopt a two-stage approach: tokenize input into verbs/nouns (e.g., "take sword" → ["take", "sword"]), then map verbs to handler functions via a dictionary dispatch pattern. Support common aliases (n/s/e/w for directions, "i" for inventory) and handle edge cases like "take all" or ambiguous nouns by validating against the current room’s contents. Avoid over-engineering the parser—prioritize covering the specified commands (go, take, drop, use, examine, talk, attack, flee, look/status/help/quit) with clear error messages for unrecognized input.

For turn-based combat, model entities (player, monsters) with base stats (health, attack, defense) modified by equipped gear. Each combat round, calculate damage as `max(1, attacker.attack - defender.defense)` to ensure progress even against high-defense foes. Give monsters simple but distinct behaviors (e.g., one always attacks, another heals on low health) via a strategy pattern or state flags. Track combat state separately from world state to handle flee/win/lose transitions cleanly. For the boss’s two phases, use a state machine: phase 1 ends when health drops below a threshold, triggering a stat boost and new attack pattern in phase 2. The weakness item (e.g., "silver dagger") can be checked mid-combat to apply bonus damage or bypass defense entirely. Avoid deep inheritance for entities—prefer composition (e.g., `CombatStats` component) to keep equipment effects and monster behaviors flexible.

data_shapes.structure: Mapping with top-level keys: rooms, items, npcs, monsters, boss, start_room_id. Rooms reference items/NPCs/monsters by id.
data_shapes.example:
rooms:
  entrance:
    title: Entrance Hall
    description: A dimly lit hall with torches on the walls.
    exits:
      north: armory
      east: garden
    items:
      - rusty_sword
    npcs: []
    monster: null
    boss: null
items:
  rusty_sword:
    id: rusty_sword
    name: Rusty Sword
    description: An old but serviceable sword.
    type: weapon
    damage: 5
  health_potion:
    id: health_potion
    name: Health Potion
    description: Restores 20 health when used.
    type: healing
    heal_amount: 20
npcs:
  guard:
    id: guard
    name: Old Guard
    description: A retired soldier with a knowing look.
    dialogue:
      - text: The boss fears the Silver Blade.
        next: 1
      - text: Find it in the treasure room.
        next: null
monsters:
  goblin:
    id: goblin
    name: Goblin
    description: A small green creature with sharp teeth.
    health: 20
    attack: 4
    defense: 1
boss:
  id: dark_knight
    name: Dark Knight
    description: A towering figure clad in black armor.
    health: 50
    attack: 8
    defense: 3
    phase2_health_threshold: 25
    phase2_attack: 12
    weakness_item: silver_blade
start_room_id: entrance

architecture.notes: Flat structure for simplicity in a small project. YAML world file is the single source of truth for content. Combat system is decoupled for testability. Save files are JSON with full state serialization.
